title: Further Competition ESPO Framework Agreement 509_23 Parking Management Solutions - AWARDED - AWARD
description:
North Hertfordshire District Council (the 'Council') is issuing this Invitation to Tender as a Further Competition under Lot 1 Pay & Display Solutions of ESPO Framework 509_23.  
      The Council would like all council managed car parks (where there are parking charges) to have new upgraded parking payment machines installed over a phased basis over a two-year financial period starting late 2023/24 and completing in 2024/25. 
      The Council is looking to replace all current pay and display machines within the car parks listed in section 2. The Council may decide to replace fewer machines than currently situated in any of the locations listed. It would therefore be the supplier's responsibility to dispose of these machines and make good the area now not required to house a machine along with any ancillary works actioned. 
      A Communications and PR campaign is essential to ensure that users are educated on the new systems with supplied resource including videos, signage, and back-office training. The successful supplier should be aware that there are different parking tariffs in operation across the council owned car parks. This includes within individual towns. There is a peak parking tariff and off-peak parking tariff in many of the towns. For example, in Royston, there is an initiative in place where parking is free from 3pm each day. And in Hitchin Town Centre, there is a flat rate after 3pm.
      The successful supplier understands the parking tariff structures in place, as well as any subsidised parking to ensure the new parking payment machines are setup correctly prior to implementation on-site. The Council requires the successful supplier to outline the process for tariff adjustments during the contract period, to ensure this meets with the Council's requirements.  
      
      This project has now been awarded.

title: NHDC01133773
description:
This public sector decarbonisation project is split over the following two sites in North Hertfordshire:
•	Hitchin Town Hall and North Herts Museum, Brand St, Hitchin SG5 1HX
•	North Herts Leisure Centre, Baldock Rd, Letchworth Garden City SG6 2ER

Hitchin Town Hall and North Herts Museum
The project is to provide improvement to Hitchin Town Hall and North Herts Museum with particular emphasis on the reduction of energy and carbon use in its operation. Funding for the decarbonisation works is partly being provided via the Salix Public Sector Decarbonisation Grant Scheme to support the North Herts Council commitment to Net Zero operations by 2030.
In order to provide improvements in the energy use of the building, the following works are proposed:
•	Installation of new secondary glazing within the window reveals of existing windows.
•	Installation of insulation within the rood void above the Main Hall of the Town Hall.
•	Installation of new Photovoltaic (PV) panels on the main roof of the Museum building.
•	Installation of new PV panels to the eastern face of the roof of the education room of the Museum.
•	Replace the existing gas fired plant with air source heat pump technology & modify existing heating systems accordingly.
•	Replacement of existing Air Handling equipment within Town Hall and museum building.

Replacement Chiller Works at Hitchin Town Hall and North Herts Museum
In addition, the following works are proposed at Hitchin Town Hall:
•	Replacement chiller with expanded capacity.
•	Multi-split DX system for the education centre and the office on the museum side of the building.
•	A cooling coil for the main hall Air Handing Unit (AHU4).
•	Installation of air conditioning to Lucas room and 1st floor office.

North Herts Leisure Centre
The project is to provide reduction of energy and carbon us in the operation of the Learner Pool at North Herts Leisure Centre. Funding for the decarbonisation works is partly being provided via the Salix Public Sector Decarbonisation Grant Scheme to support the North Herts Council commitment to Net Zero operations by 2030.

In order to provide improvements in the energy use of the building, the following works are proposed:
•	Replace the existing gas fired boiler plant with air source heat pump technology & modify existing heating systems for the Learner Pool.
•	Provide an enclosure for the ASHP units to minimise visual impact and noise for visitors and neighbours of the site.
•	Provide screening planting to minimise the visual impact of the fencing around the ASHP units.

The Hitchin Town Hall and North Herts Museum and North Herts Leisure Centre will be delivering under a single JCT Design & Build contract.
Please note that the replacement chiller works will be delivered under a separate JCT Design & Build contact.

title: Contract for the Provision of Coroner's Post Mortems
description:
This is an Award Notice. Hertfordshire County Council have awarded a contract for the Provision of Coroner's Post Mortems. There is no competition for this service. Deceased bodies referred to the Hertfordshire Coroner must remain within their jurisdiction until officially released by the Hertfordshire Coroner.

Hertfordshire County Council (HCC) is relying on Regulation 32(2)(b)(ii) of the Public Contract Regulations 2015 in making this award without prior publication. Regulation 32(2)(b)(ii) permits such an award where competition is absent for technical reasons.

The Local Authority has a statutory duty to provide a Coroner Service for the community of Hertfordshire.  As part of the Coroner's duties, he/she must establish a cause of death if none has been provided by the signing/authorising medical practitioner.  

To facilitate post-mortem examinations Hertfordshire County Council has contracts with local NHS Hospital mortuaries.  There are 3 NHS Hospital mortuaries within Hertfordshire (or close to the Hertfordshire border) that provide post-mortem services to the Coroner Service.  Currently, one mortuary would not be able to manage the volume of post-mortems requested by Hertfordshire so we need more than one contract to cover this requirement.

The direct award value of £980,000 reflects the total estimated value that will be awarded over the whole term of the contract between the three NHS trusts receiving the direct award.  The £980,000 will not be equally divided between the three NHS trusts but will be awarded based on volume of deceased sent to each NHS trust for coronial post-mortem examination each month.

Reg 32(2)(b) states that a procurement is not required where a service can only be supplied by a particular economic operator ENHT, WHHT and PAH in this case because "competition is absent for technical reasons".
